explanation: Pan, the goat-legged god of shepherds and wild places, was said to fill lonely travellers with sudden, groundless fear. Phobos, the Greek word and god of fear, gave English phobia.

claims.text: 'Panic' comes from Greek panikos, 'of Pan', after the god Pan.
'Panic' does not come from the names of Ares, Hermes or Phobos.
Pan was the goat-legged Greek god of shepherds and wild places, believed to cause sudden fear in lonely places.
'Phobia' comes from Greek phobos, 'fear', also personified as a god.
